added.long_description:
Alchemize is a code review platform that helps teams understand PRs and ship faster.

Agentic coding has 10x’d code output. Teams are opening larger PRs more frequently, but the current tools don’t support this new coding paradigm. 

Alchemize automatically breaks down PRs into guided, understandable reviews. It breaks each PR into manageable, smaller PRs that reveals the original author’s (human or agent) intent. We show where changes begin, how data flows, and which decisions require human judgment.
added.one_liner: Code Review Platform that Simplifies PRs to Ship Faster

added.name: Tenor
added.long_description:
Your AI spend becomes accountable labor: every AI worker gets a job, persistent context, a budget, guardrails, and outcomes you can measure.

Copilots made individuals faster. Agent builders made automations easier to create. Both leave the organization unchanged: same roles, same capacity, same org chart, and leadership still sees AI as a software expense, not labor. 

Tenor makes AI enter the company as labor instead: every employee manages a team of AI workers built around the recurring work of their role, each with a defined job, boundaries, a budget, and a record of what it delivered. Employees provide the judgment. AI workers provide the execution. Leadership finally sees what AI spend returns.
added.one_liner: Turn every employee into a manager of AI workers

added.name: Hemlock
added.long_description:
Every serious robotics lab is bottlenecked on the same thing: demonstration data. The field has converged on egocentric video and hand pose as the substrate, and both are now cheap to collect at scale. What neither of them contains is force. A video of someone picking up an egg and a video of someone picking up a rock are nearly identical in pixel space and nearly identical in joint angles. They differ almost entirely in a quantity nobody is recording. Policies trained without it learn geometry and inherit no sense of touch.

Hemlock closes that gap at the source. Our device, the Bracelet, is a wrist-worn surface EMG band that reads the electrical activity of the forearm muscles that actually drive the hand, which means it recovers contraction force directly rather than inferring it from motion. This distinction is the whole thesis: force cannot be reconstructed downstream of kinematics, because a hand squeezing hard isometrically and a hand resting can occupy the identical pose. Muscle signal is the only non-invasive channel that separates them.
added.one_liner: Force-sensing wristband for training robotic AI

Your agent processed a refund without looking up the order ID, costing you thousands. You only found out three hours later from a support ticket. Evals, output scoring, and observability can reduce the likelihood of mistakes like these occurring - but there's no solution that inspects and prevents an action as it’s about to execute. Salus does that.

We’ve built an API that wraps around your agent and checks its actions at run time, blocking incorrect ones and providing immediate feedback to guide retries. Kevin and Vedant were roommates at Stanford, where they both studied computer science.

We build collaborative robot squads for solar farm construction.

High labor costs, labor shortages, and unpredictable productivity make infrastructure difficult to build in places that are remote, harsh, or empty. We are building robots to unlock places once considered too difficult to develop. Solar is our first proving ground, spanning utility-scale, commercial and industrial, community solar, agrivoltaic, and other projects.

Unlike solutions that automate only one task, or even part of one, we cover the workflow after PV module pallets arrive on-site: transportation, installation, alignment, and fastening. Each robot has a specific role, and fleets can be configured based on each project’s cost and schedule requirements.

Our robots operate autonomously with remote supervision. One person can supervise 4+ robots through a screen and an e-stop button, without being physically present or teleoperating them. Our robotic fleet has also been tested at night, paving the way for 24/7 operation.

We work directly with EPCs through a Robotics-as-a-Service model, requiring no robot purchase or large upfront capital investment. We also work with racking and PV module manufacturers to certify compatibility and give customers confidence in deployment.

Purpose-built hardware, multimodal sensing, and physical AI software help our robots handle real-world construction uncertainty.

one_liner.before: Autonomous robots for solar farm construction
one_liner.after: Multi-robot collaboration for harsh environments on Earth.
